passage:
Every night after the shop closed, Tanuja sat on the back steps with her phone and called Zeenat, who taught at the girls' school across town. She talked about the dreams she'd never said aloud: a small tailoring class of her own, a trip to the sea. Zeenat listened and asked real questions.

With Sameer, she talked about rice and electricity bills. When he asked who she was speaking to, she said, "Just a friend," and turned the screen away.

One evening she caught herself editing a story so that Sameer wouldn't hear the parts she'd given Zeenat. "Just a friend" wasn't the whole truth; it was the door she'd shut.

She sat with that. What she wanted was for Sameer to ask about the tailoring class. The next day she said, "Will you listen to something I've never told you?"

qa.q: What did Tanuja talk about with Zeenat every night?
qa.a: She talked about dreams she had never said aloud, like a small tailoring class of her own and a trip to the sea.

qa.q: What was Tanuja feeling when she turned the screen away and said 'Just a friend'?
qa.a: She felt a need to keep her closeness with Zeenat hidden, along with an uneasy sense that she was concealing something from Sameer.

qa.q: What could Tanuja do about what is missing at home?
qa.a: Share her dreams with Sameer directly and see whether they can talk about more than bills, and be honest about what she needs.

qa.q: How might Sameer feel if he only found out later that she shared her dreams with Zeenat?
qa.a: He might feel shut out and hurt, and wonder why she never offered him the same trust.

grounding: Shows sharing deeper feelings with someone else than with a partner, hidden as just a friend, then noticed and brought to the partner.

passage: Darshan, you're my oldest friend, so I'll just say it. I'm Pankaj, and I think I've been cheating on Ruchi without ever touching anyone. There's a woman in my office, Neha. It started with lunch. Then long chats every night. I tell her things I've never told Ruchi: how scared I am about my father's health, how much I hate my job. Whenever Ruchi asks who I'm texting, I say 'just work'. That's the part that gave it away. If it were really just friendship, why hide it? Last week Neha said, 'You talk to me the way you should talk to her.' That hit hard. So I've been thinking about what's missing with Ruchi. We stopped really talking months ago. It became dinners and plans and nothing underneath. I'm going to tell her the truth, all of it, and tell her what I've been missing. Maybe we can fix it. Maybe we end it honestly. But I'm done calling this 'just friendship'.

qa.q: What does Pankaj tell Ruchi when she asks who he's texting?
How did Pankaj feel when Neha said he talked to her the way he should talk to Ruchi?
qa.a: It hit him hard, leaving him guilty and uneasy about what he'd been hiding.

qa.q: What is Pankaj planning to do?
qa.a: Tell Ruchi the full truth and what he's been missing, then either work on it together or end it honestly.

qa.q: How might Ruchi feel when she learns about the nightly chats?
qa.a: Hurt and shut out, since he shared his fears with someone else instead of her.

grounding: A spoken account of a young man sharing deeper feelings with a colleague than with his partner, noticing what's missing and choosing honesty over calling it friendship.

passage: July. Himani's boyfriend, Nikhil, was in Bengaluru for work, and their calls had shrunk to 'Ate? Slept? Okay, bye.' In the college library, Uday started sitting at her table. They talked about books, then about her fear of failing her thesis, then about her parents' divorce, which she had never really discussed with Nikhil. August. She caught herself hiding her screen when Uday's messages came in, and telling Nikhil she'd been 'studying alone'. One night she typed to Uday, 'You understand me better than anyone,' and felt her stomach drop as she sent it. September. Himani stopped telling herself it was just friendship. She told Uday she needed distance. Then she called Nikhil and said, 'I've been sharing things with someone else that I should have been sharing with you. I need us to really talk, or to be honest that it isn't working.' There was a long silence. Then Nikhil said, 'I've felt it too. Let's talk properly this weekend.'

qa.q: What did Himani feel when she sent the message to Uday?
qa.a: Her stomach dropped with guilt as she sent it.

qa.q: What did Himani do once she stopped calling it just friendship?
qa.a: Asked Uday for distance and told Nikhil honestly what had happened and what was missing, asking to really talk.

qa.q: How has Nikhil been experiencing the relationship?
qa.a: He admits he has felt the distance too and wants to talk properly.

grounding: Shows a young woman sharing deeper feelings with a classmate than with her partner, then admitting it and talking honestly about what's missing.
